gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Godox's newer V1 mid round-head flash takes the AK-R1 magnetic round-head accessories (whose dome is the one the AK-R11 matches) but comes only in C/N/S/F/O versions, so Panasonic (P) shooters still need the V1-P. None of them says that a flash for one camera brand will not do TTL on another.
standout_why: I compared against B&H's AK-R11 pages (the one ChatGPT cited), Camera Canada GO-AK-R11 (result 5) and Godox's flash FAQ (result 7), and read cameraegg's 'Best Diffuser for Godox V1' (result 13). B&H's specs page and manuals.plus returned 403, so I could not open them. Camera Canada already says the dome 'fits the round head V1 directly', fits the AD200/AD200 Pro with the H200R adapter, and 'fits the TT685 speedlight using the optional SR-1 round head adapter'. The Godox FAQ says the S-R1 lets the magnetic dome mount on a V860II. So the adapter fact for rectangular-head speedlights is already in the rival set. None of the rival pages I opened mentions the V1 mid. None lists which camera-system versions each flash comes in, and none points out that the V1 mid has no Panasonic version. Cameraegg names no flash other than the V1.
decides: The answer holds: a Godox round-head flash plus the magnetic dome is the simplest diffuser setup, because the dome mounts with no adapter. Godox names the V1 (C/N/S/F/O/P) and the V1 mid (C/N/S/F/O) as round-head flashes for its AK-R1 accessories. The newer V1 mid is the current option for Canon, Nikon, Sony, Fujifilm and Olympus/OM bodies. Panasonic users should pick the V1-P. A TT685II or V860III owner needs the separate S-R1 adapter before any round dome will fit. ChatGPT asked 'What camera do you use?', and the camera brand is what decides which flash version to buy.

The page links a 'Compatible Camera Model List' PDF whose contents I did not read.
